topics: 🍞 Kuba De'ara — the dough of the ground: mezonot, unless like Mar Zutra you base your meal on it; and it counts as 'bread of affliction'
🍯 Date Honey vs. Pressed Dates — mere moisture gets shehakol, terima keeps ha'etz; Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on teruma juices
🥣 Shetita — Rav vs. Shmuel; Rav Ḥisda's thick and thin; is a medicinal drink permitted on Shabbat and does it need a blessing?
📖 Hamotzi or Motzi — Rabbi Neḥemya vs. the Rabbis on past and present tense, and the guest who dodged the dispute
🥬 Boiled Vegetables — Rav and Shmuel say ha'adama, Ulla in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name says shehakol, Rav Ḥisda splits the difference
🫒 Which Rabbi Yoḥanan? — Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba vs. Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet, the seven-boiled lupin, and the salted olive

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Cooked, Pressed, and Boiled
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 38a–38b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues the chapter's tour of foods that have been transformed. A dough roasted in the ground is not bread, unless someone treats it as the basis of a meal; date honey is only 'sweat' of the fruit, but dates pressed into a cake are still dates; a barley drink is food when thick and medicine when thin, yet either way it earns a blessing because one enjoys it. Then the mishna's own word hamotzi comes under scrutiny: does it mean 'brings forth' or 'brought forth', and the halakha settles on hamotzi. The second amud takes up boiled vegetables, where the Babylonian tradition (ha'adama) faces Ulla's report of Rabbi Yoḥanan (shehakol), and Rabbi Zeira must decide which of Rabbi Yoḥanan's students transmitted him accurately.

slides.title: 🧾 Transformed Foods and Their Blessings
slides.subtitle: The daf's opening rulings, each turning on whether the food is still 'itself'
rows: Kuba de'ara, dough roasted in the ground
Rav Yosef to Abaye: בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת
'Do you think it is bread? It is mere kneaded dough'
Same, when one bases a meal on it
Basing a meal on it makes it bread; Mar bar Rav Ashi: it even fulfills matza, being 'bread of affliction'
'It is mere moisture' — like Rabbi Yehoshua, who exempts one who ate teruma date honey, apple wine or fruit juice from the fifth; Rabbi Eliezer obligates
'They remain in their original state'; Rav Asi permits making terima from teruma dates but not beer
Shetita, roasted barley with honey or vinegar
Rav Ḥisda: no dispute — thick is made as food (mezonot), thin as medicine (shehakol)

callout.label: A word Rava did not know:
callout.text: A student asked Rava about terima; Rava did not recognize the term until Ravina asked the student whether he meant sesame, safflower, or grape-pit terima, at which point Rava recalled Rav Asi's ruling.

slides.title: 🥣 Shetita: Medicine, Food, and the Need for a Blessing
slides.subtitle: Rav Yosef attacks Rav Ḥisda's 'thin = medicine' from the laws of Shabbat

nodes.content: 📜 Rav Ḥisda: thick shetita is food → mezonot (Shmuel); thin shetita is medicine → shehakol (Rav)
❓ Rav Yosef: a mishna says all agree one may stir shetita on Shabbat and drink Egyptian beer. If it were medicine, is medicine permitted on Shabbat?

💡 Abaye: a mishna permits eating any ordinary food or drink for healing on Shabbat — because the person's intention is eating. Here too his intention is eating (another version: eating, and the cure comes by itself)
❓ Then it is plainly food — why did Rav and Shmuel need to say a blessing is required?

✅ Necessary: the Shabbat mishna covers one who intends to eat. Here he intends healing from the outset, and one might think medicine needs no blessing. Rav and Shmuel teach: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ בָּעֵי בָּרוֹכֵי — since he enjoys it, he must bless

slides.title: 📖 Hamotzi or Motzi? A Blessing Hangs on a Tense
slides.subtitle: The Rabbis vs. Rabbi Neḥemya, as explained by Rava, and a guest who played it safe

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: What does one say over bread? הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ. Rabbi Neḥemya says: מוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ.

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: All agree motzi means 'brought forth' in the past: 'God who brought them forth (מוֹצִיאָם) from Egypt' (Num. 23:22). They dispute hamotzi.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: Hamotzi also means 'brought forth': 'Who brought forth (הַמּוֹצִיא) for you water from the flint rock' (Deut. 8:15).

lines.speaker: R' Neḥemya
lines.text: Hamotzi means 'is bringing forth', present tense: 'I am the Lord your God who is bringing you forth (הַמּוֹצִיא) from under the burdens of Egypt' (Ex. 6:7) — unfit for a blessing about the past.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: That verse means: when I bring you out, I will do something so that you will know that I am the One who brought you out — past tense after all.

lines.speaker: R' Zeira
lines.text: The Sages praised the son of Rav Zevid as an expert in blessings. When he came and said motzi, Rabbi Zeira scoffed: had he said hamotzi he would have taught us the verse's meaning and that the halakha follows the Rabbis. What did motzi teach? Answer: he chose it to keep himself out of the dispute.

callout.label: Halakha:
callout.text: וְהִלְכְתָא ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״ — we follow the Rabbis, for whom hamotzi also means 'brought forth'.

slides.title: 🥬 Boiled Vegetables (Shelakot): Three Positions
slides.subtitle: The mishna lists vegetables next to bread — does cooking change their blessing?

boxes.title: Babylonia: Ha'adama
items: Rabbenai in Abaye's name: vegetables are taught alongside bread — just as bread is transformed by fire, vegetables keep ha'adama after fire
Rav Ḥisda in the name of 'Rabbeinu' (Rav): boiled vegetables → בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה
Rav Naḥman in the name of 'Rabbeinu' (Shmuel): the same

boxes.title: From Eretz Yisrael: Shehakol
items: Ulla in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name: boiled vegetables → שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיֶה בִּדְבָרוֹ
Boiling changes them; they are no longer what they were
Rav Naḥman proposed it mirrors R' Meir vs. R' Yosei on boiled matza — the Gemara rejects this: R' Yosei only demands the taste of matza

boxes.title: Rav Ḥisda's Own View
items: What is ha'adama raw becomes shehakol boiled — Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: garlic and leeks
What is shehakol raw becomes ha'adama boiled — cabbage, chard, pumpkin, inedible until cooked
Cooking can improve or damage; the blessing follows the result

callout.label: Conclusion of the Gemara:
callout.text: Everyone agrees boiled vegetables get ha'adama; the matza dispute is about taste, not about whether boiling ruins a food.

slides.title: 🫒 Did Rabbi Yoḥanan Really Say Shehakol? Rabbi Zeira Weighs the Witnesses
slides.subtitle: Two students, one master, and the evidence of a lupin and a salted olive

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba reports Rabbi Yoḥanan: boiled vegetables → ha'adama. Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet reports him: shehakol. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: Ulla fixed his error by following Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet
2️⃣ Rabbi Zeira: what is Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet doing beside Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba? The latter was meticulous in learning from his teacher; the former was not
3️⃣ Furthermore, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba reviewed his learning before Rabbi Yoḥanan every thirty days; Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet did not
4️⃣ Furthermore, a lupin boiled seven times and eaten as dessert — they asked Rabbi Yoḥanan, and he said ha'adama

5️⃣ Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba adds: I saw Rabbi Yoḥanan eat a salted olive and bless before and after. If cooked food stays itself: ha'etz before, me'ein shalosh after. If not: shehakol before — but what after? Rejected: perhaps he said borei nefashot

6️⃣ Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Shmuel objects: for bitter herbs on Passover one may use the vegetables and stalks but not pickled, boiled or cooked ones! Answer: there we need the taste of maror, and it is lacking

callout.label: Cliffhanger:
callout.text: Rabbi Yirmeya asks Rabbi Zeira how Rabbi Yoḥanan could bless after a salted olive at all, since the pit was removed and not eaten — the question continues on the next daf.

summary.principle: A food keeps its blessing as long as it remains what it was — pressed dates, thick barley drink, boiled vegetables all stay themselves — and enjoyment, not intent, is what obligates a blessing.

flowSteps.content: 🍞 Kuba de'ara → mezonot; based a meal on it (Mar Zutra) → hamotzi and three blessings; it is 'bread of affliction' for matza
🍯 Date honey = moisture → shehakol (like R' Yehoshua on teruma juices); terima keeps ha'etz; shetita thick → mezonot, thin → shehakol, and either way one blesses because one enjoys it
❓ Hamotzi or motzi? Rabbis: hamotzi also means 'brought forth'; R' Neḥemya: present tense. Halakha: hamotzi

columns.content: 🥬 Boiled vegetables: Rav & Shmuel ha'adama; Ulla in R' Yoḥanan's name shehakol; Rav Ḥisda: depends on raw vs. cooked edibility
🫒 R' Zeira: trust R' Ḥiyya bar Abba over R' Binyamin bar Yefet — the seven-boiled lupin and the salted olive show R' Yoḥanan said ha'adama

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Everyone agrees boiled vegetables get borei peri ha'adama; the maror and matza rules differ only because they require a specific taste

quiz.q: Why does Mar bar Rav Ashi rule that one recites shehakol over date honey?
o: Because honey is never eaten alone
Because it is mere moisture that drips from the fruit, not the fruit itself
Because dates are not among the seven species
Because it is made only outside Eretz Yisrael
quiz.e: Date honey is 'mere sweat' of the fruit. The Gemara links this to Rabbi Yehoshua, who exempts one who ate teruma date honey or fruit juice from the added fifth because such juices are byproducts, not the fruit.

quiz.q: How does Rav Ḥisda reconcile Rav (shehakol) and Shmuel (mezonot) regarding shetita?
o: Rav speaks of barley, Shmuel of wheat
Rav speaks of a thin mixture made as medicine, Shmuel of a thick one made as food
Rav speaks of Shabbat, Shmuel of weekdays
Rav retracted after Rav Yosef's objection
quiz.e: They do not disagree: a thick shetita is prepared as food and gets mezonot; a thin one is prepared as medicine and gets shehakol.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, why did the son of Rav Zevid recite motzi rather than hamotzi?
o: He held like Rabbi Neḥemya that hamotzi is present tense
He was not actually expert in blessings
He wished to remove himself from the dispute, since motzi is valid according to all
Rabbi Zeira had instructed him to do so
quiz.e: Rabbi Zeira was disappointed that the guest taught nothing new. The Gemara explains he deliberately chose the formula acceptable to everyone, so as not to take sides. The halakha nonetheless is hamotzi.

quiz.q: Which vegetables does Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak give as examples of foods that are ha'adama raw but shehakol when boiled, according to Rav Ḥisda's view?
o: Cabbage and chard
Pumpkin and lupin
Garlic and leeks
Radish and heart of palm
quiz.e: Rav Ḥisda's intermediate view says boiling can damage a vegetable normally eaten raw. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak identifies garlic and leeks; cabbage, chard and pumpkin are the opposite case, improved by boiling.

quiz.q: What was one of Rabbi Zeira's reasons for preferring Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba's report of Rabbi Yoḥanan over Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet's?
o: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba reviewed his learning before Rabbi Yoḥanan every thirty days
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba was older
Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet lived in Babylonia
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba was Rabbi Yoḥanan's son
quiz.e: Rabbi Zeira gave three grounds: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba was meticulous, he reviewed his studies before Rabbi Yoḥanan every thirty days, and Rabbi Yoḥanan himself ruled ha'adama over a lupin boiled seven times.
